sections.heading: Glossary term: X-ray Telescope
sections.body: An X-ray telescope is a type of telescope specially designed for the observation of high-energy, high-frequency, X-ray light that is invisible to the human eye. Since Earth's atmosphere completely absorbs incoming X-rays, X-ray telescopes are typically space telescopes. The high frequencies and correspondingly short wavelengths of X-rays require optics markedly different from those of visible-light telescopes: X-rays fall onto the telescope mirrors at very shallow angles ("grazing incidence") to bounce off the exterior of the mirror ("external reflection"). Mirror assemblies for focusing X-rays that work in this way are often built as concentric shells. At very high energies, for "hard" X-rays, telescope optics typically do not attempt to focus the light at all, but instead rely on masks to extract information about X-ray direction, and from this information reconstruct images.

sections.source_html:
Glossary term: X-ray Telescope

Description: An X-ray telescope is a type of telescope specially designed for the observation of high-energy, high-frequency, X-ray light that is invisible to the human eye. Since Earth's atmosphere completely absorbs incoming X-rays, X-ray telescopes are typically space telescopes. The high frequencies and correspondingly short wavelengths of X-rays require optics markedly different from those of visible-light telescopes: X-rays fall onto the telescope mirrors at very shallow angles ("grazing incidence") to bounce off the exterior of the mirror ("external reflection"). Mirror assemblies for focusing X-rays that work in this way are often built as concentric shells. At very high energies, for "hard" X-rays, telescope optics typically do not attempt to focus the light at all, but instead rely on masks to extract information about X-ray direction, and from this information reconstruct images.

Related Terms:

  • X-ray Astronomy
  • X-ray


See this term in other languages

Term and definition status: This term and its definition have been approved by a research astronomer and a teacher

The OAE Multilingual Glossary is a project of the IAU Office of Astronomy for Education (OAE) in collaboration with the IAU Office of Astronomy Outreach (OAO). The terms and definitions were chosen, written and reviewed by a collective effort from the OAE, the OAE Centers and Nodes, the OAE National Astronomy Education Coordinators (NAECs) and other volunteers. You can find a full list of credits here. All glossary terms and their definitions are released under a Creative Commons CC BY-4.0 license and should be credited to "IAU OAE".

If you notice a factual error in this glossary definition then please get in touch.
sections.body_ru: Рентгеновский телескоп — это тип телескопа, специально разработанный для наблюдения высокоэнергетического, высокочастотного рентгеновского излучения, невидимого для человеческого глаза. Поскольку атмосфера Земли полностью поглощает приходящие из космоса рентгеновские лучи, рентгеновские телескопы обычно являются космическими телескопами. Высокие частоты и соответственно короткие длины волн рентгеновских лучей требуют оптики, заметно отличающейся от оптики телескопов видимого света: рентгеновские лучи падают на зеркала телескопа под очень малыми углами («скользящее падение»), чтобы отражаться от внешней поверхности зеркала («внешнее отражение»). Системы зеркал для фокусировки рентгеновских лучей, работающие таким образом, часто выполняют в виде концентрических оболочек. При очень высоких энергиях, в диапазоне «жёсткого» рентгеновского излучения, обычно вообще не используют фокусирующую оптику, а применяют маски для получения информации о направлении прихода рентгеновских лучей и на основе этой информации восстанавливают изображения.
